title: Declarative function-call schema versioning and SDK compatibility shim
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Context: We need a maintainable, versioned JSON schema format for function/tool calling parameters plus a compatibility shim to handle older SDK shapes. The goal is to support strict validation for new clients while providing a progressive compatibility path for customers on older SDKs and reduce incidents caused by ambiguous error messages.

Problem summary:
- Current validation returns opaque textual errors or a single HTTP 400 with a message. This causes confusion in customer apps and poor observability in the Console.
- SDKs in the wild send slightly different shapes (flattened args, snake_case vs camelCase, omitted optional objects). There is no declarative mapping table.
- Streaming/tool calls with very large param payloads need partial validation feedback so callers can surface user-friendly hints while the model is still generating.

Proposed design (high-level):
1) Schema envelope: every function/tool registration includes a small envelope with metadata and the canonical JSON Schema draft-07-like body. Envelope fields: "schema_id", "schema_version", "compatibility_policy" (one of: strict, lenient, coerce), "deprecated_fields" (list). Example as text:
  {
    "schema_id": "com.redwood.payment.create_order",
    "schema_version": "2026-02-01",
    "compatibility_policy": "lenient",
    "schema": { /* standard JSON Schema */ }
  }

2) Validation modes (server-side):
  - strict: reject any violation with structured errors (HTTP 400).
  - warn: accept payload, return warnings array with structured validation codes and a 200.
  - coerce: attempt mild coercions (string->number where sensible, case mapping), record transformations in response metadata.

3) Structured error taxonomy and shape (always returned in responses as JSON metadata). Error codes: INVALID_TYPE, MISSING_REQUIRED, UNEXPECTED_FIELD, ENUM_MISMATCH, FORMAT_ERROR, DEPRECATION_WARNING. Error fields: code, path (JSON Pointer), message, suggestion, example.
Note: This ticket defines the error taxonomy and examples; serialization is handled by runtime infra in ENG-20712.

4) Compatibility shim (server-side mapping rules):
  - Declarative mapping rules can be provided in the envelope: e.g., map {"user_id": "userId", "amt_cents": "amount.cents"}. Mappings are applied in coerce/lenient modes only.
  - Legacy flattening/unflattening helpers: if schema expects {payment:{amount:{value}}} and incoming has {payment_amount_value}, use mapping rules to fold fields.
  - Deprecation metadata: when a field is deprecated, include DEPRECATION_WARNING with removal ETA in messages.

5) Streaming partial validation: for requests flagged with header X-Validation-Stream: true, the runtime will emit incremental validation frames during streaming responses. Each frame is small JSON (validation_warnings/validation_errors) that clients can display. Frames use the same structured error schema and include path offsets for very large arrays.

Acceptance criteria:
- Formal schema envelope format documented and added to function registry API docs.
- Server implements strict/warn/coerce modes and returns structured errors per taxonomy.
- Compatibility mapping rules are supported and applied in coerce mode.
- Streaming partial validation frames are emitted when requested.
- Console surfaces: per-route validation error counts, top error codes, and example failing payloads in Observability.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Full UI in Console for editing mapping rules (follow-up).
- Advanced coercions (e.g., natural-language parsing to typed objects) — future work for Eval team.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement server-side validation + taxonomy behind a feature flag.
2) Add a public docs page (function-calling schema) and SDK v2 release notes.
3) Enable warn mode by default for hosted endpoints; strict mode opt-in per customer until 2026-05-01.

Monitoring and metrics to add:
- validation.error.count by code
- validation.warn.count
- validation.coercions.count
- validation.latency

Additional notes:
- Keep the schema format minimal — we prefer relying on standard JSON Schema facets but add a thin Redwood metadata layer for versioning and compat rules.
- Security: validation code must not evaluate untrusted expressions. No use of eval or JS function compilation.
acceptance_criteria: Schema envelope format published in docs (Confluence link in links).
Server returns structured errors with code/path/message for strict mode failures.
Warn mode accepts payloads and returns warnings array in response metadata.
Coerce mode applies declared mapping rules and records transformations in response metadata.
Streaming validation frames emitted when X-Validation-Stream: true header is present.
decisions: Use JSON Schema as the canonical ruleset and add a lightweight Redwood envelope for metadata.
Expose three modes (strict|warn|coerce) to balance safety and compatibility.
Structured error taxonomy chosen to make Console aggregation and SDK surface predictable.
implementation_notes: Validate using an existing, audited JSON Schema library (no eval) and compile schemas at registration time.
Store schema_id -> compiled schema in function registry to avoid runtime compilation costs.
Apply mapping rules as a deterministic transform before validation when in coerce/lenient modes.
For streaming validation, reuse the same validator but emit errors as scanning proceeds (support partial arrays).
test_plan: Unit tests: each error code must map to specific schema violation scenarios.
Integration: register sample schema and exercise strict/warn/coerce modes with real SDK payloads.
E2E streaming test: send a large array payload and assert validation frames are emitted with correct offsets.
Monitoring: add tests that increment metrics and assert counts are emitted.
